import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided by the user
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the scatter plot (bubble chart)
# x-axis: Megapixels
# y-axis: Price
# Bubble size: Max ISO
# Bubble color: Sensor Type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    size='max_iso',
    hue='sensor_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Control the min and max size of bubbles
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax,
    palette='magma'
)

# Add annotations for each point to provide more context
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(
        row['megapixels'] + 0.5,
        row['price_usd'],
        f"{row['brand']} ({row['model_year']})",
        fontdict={'size': 10, 'weight': 'semibold'}
    )

# --- Customize the plot for clarity and insight ---

# Set plot title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Camera Analysis: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Format y-axis to show dollar signs
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}'))

# Adjust axis limits to give some padding
ax.set_xlim(df['megapixels'].min() - 5, df['megapixels'].max() + 5)
ax.set_ylim(0, df['price_usd'].max() * 1.1)

# Improve the legend
h, l = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the hue and size legends and give them titles
plt.legend(h[1:5], l[1:5], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0., title='Sensor Type', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Manually add a legend for size as the default can be complex
size_legend_handles = [plt.scatter([], [], s=s/10, c='gray', alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black') for s in [6400, 25600, 51200]]
size_legend_labels = ['6,400', '25,600', '51,200']
ax.add_artist(plt.legend(size_legend_handles, size_legend_labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6), loc='upper left', title='Max ISO', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12))

# Ensure everything fits well within the figure
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for legends

# Save the resulting plot
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
